rationale: Contract table row: contract.md:116 "| btrfs | … exactly one uuid, `qgroups` false | disabled | n/a | `btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent` |", read with contract.md:115 (the … row is the same single-uuid row with qgroups true) and contract.md:117 (zero/several uuids -> `btrfs_device_unmapped`, which does not apply here because exactly one uuid lists the device). Mount resolution: contract.md:95-99 — mountinfo parsed per proc.rst §3.5 (S082: proc.rst:1973-1983 field table; field 3 major:minor at :1975, separator (m+1) at :1980, filesystem type (m+2) at :1981, mount source (m+3) at :1982, super options (m+4) at :1983). Candidates for /opt/mori/quota-case: the "/" btrfs mount (mount point equals "/") and the "/home" btrfs mount (rejected: realpath does not start with "/home/"); longest mount point wins, so the chosen mount is "/" (fstype btrfs, source /dev/mapper/root, super options "rw,space_cache,subvolid=5,subvol=/"). Device check: contract.md:100-103 — the `device_mismatch` basis applies only when the chosen fstype is not btrfs; for btrfs the st_dev of the path here equals the mount major:minor 0:26, so the equal branch gives device_check "match"; S081 (fs/btrfs/inode.c:8246, `stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev;`) shows the usual btrfs case is a per-subvolume anonymous device and therefore a mismatch, i.e. this case deliberately exercises the defensive equal branch that S081 neither proves reachable nor forbids. Quota classification: the mount source basename /dev/mapper/root maps through device_links to device dm-0, and exactly one uuid ("8f3c1d2e-4b5a-4c6d-9e8f-0a1b2c3d4e5f") lists dm-0 in its devices, with qgroups false, so the row at contract.md:116 applies: quota_state disabled, enforcement n/a, basis btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent (S079, fs/btrfs/sysfs.c qgroup_enabled_show:2355-2368 / qgroups attribute group:2450-2461, for the sysfs presence/absence surface; S080, fs/btrfs/qgroup.c btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups:1032 / btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups:620,689,1295, for why the absent directory does not prove quota was never possible — the disabled reading is a visibility statement, not a claim that limits exist or never existed). Verdict: contract.md:132-134 — no path is enabled and no path is unknown, so exit 0 and finding_id QUOTA_DISABLED. Expected-key discipline: the expected path object carries exactly the six compared facets (path, fstype, mount_point, quota_state, enforcement, basis) per contract.md:124-128 and the sealed-case comparison rule "per-path (path, fstype, mount_point, quota_state, enforcement, basis)"; the output-only tokens device_check, quota_option_keys and btrfs_qgroups_mode are deliberately absent from `expected`, so this case places no requirement on the device_check token value (it would be "match" here) nor on quota_option_keys (btrfs super options carry no quota key) nor on btrfs_qgroups_mode (null).
